paper_title: Astrophysical limits on very light axion-like particles from Chandra grating spectroscopy of NGC 1275
notes: Reynolds et al. 2020 (ApJ), Chandra HETG spectroscopy of NGC 1275. Headline result is a limit on the ALP-photon coupling g_agamma from the absence of X-ray spectral distortions (photon-ALP conversion in the cluster magnetic field); this is an X-ray transparency measurement, independent of ALP dark-matter density, so dm_density_assumed=null. Confidence level is the 99.7% credible region (marginalized over magnetic-field realizations), as the paper states (not 0.90/0.95). Two magnetic-field models are shown: Model-A gives g<6.3e-13 GeV^-1 and Model-B (boxed Eq. 5) gives g<7.9e-13 GeV^-1 for m_a<1e-12 eV. I report the more conservative Model-B curve (bottom panel of Fig. 6, HETG 99.7% excl. heavy black line); the two models' flat levels agree to ~25% so the choice is well within factor-2 scoring. Curve traced by pixel analysis of the embedded raster figure f6b_new.pdf: flat at ~7.9e-13 GeV^-1 for m_a below ~2e-13 eV, then a jagged rise above ~2e-13 eV peaking near ~3.1e-12 GeV^-1 and terminating around 5e-12 eV. Axis calibration from x labels (10^-20..10^-8 eV) and y labels (10^-13..10^-11 GeV^-1). Flat left extent set to the plotted range; the paper states the limit is insensitive to the minimum ALP mass.
